findings.title: newGameResets passes with newGameButtonTapped as a no-op
findings.failure_scenario: On this branch Game.play(at:) is an empty stub (Packages/AppFeature/Sources/GameCore/Game.swift:35-36), so `played` equals Game(). If GameFeature.swift:42 (`state.game = Game()`) is removed, the state stays Game(), which matches the expected Game(), and the test still passes. On this branch it can't catch a stale board after a restart. Once ttt-rules lands a real play(at:), `played` holds X at 4 and the same test does catch a dropped reset.
findings.evidence:
GameFeatureTests.swift:15-20: `var played = Game(); played.play(at: 4)` ... `send(.newGameButtonTapped) { $0.game = Game() }`. Game.swift:35-36: `public mutating func play(at cell: Int) {
  }`. GameFeature.swift:42: `state.game = Game()`.
findings.fix: Build the non-empty starting state without relying on Game.play, for example with a test-only Game initializer or by asserting played != Game() first, so the test fails when the reset is dropped. Alternatively make it depend on the ttt-rules merge.
findings.verification_note: Read GameFeatureTests.swift, GameFeature.swift and GameCore/Game.swift in the worktree. play(at:) has an empty body, so `played == Game()`, and the reset assertion compares Game() with Game() whether or not the reducer resets. I confirmed the test can't fail on this branch. I lowered the severity to minor because the gap is temporary: the plan builds the rules in parallel (ttt-rules), and once play(at:) is real the same test catches a dropped reset with no change. No user-facing behavior is affected.

findings.title: cellTapPlays and invalidTapsIgnored assert against the same stubbed Game.play
findings.failure_scenario: On this branch Game.play is a no-op, so in cellTapPlays `expected` is Game(). Removing `state.game.play(at: index)` (GameFeature.swift:40), or forwarding the wrong index, leaves the state at Game(), which equals expected, so the test passes. invalidTapsIgnored sends taps that change nothing, so it passes whether or not taps are forwarded. Both tests prove nothing about tap forwarding on this branch.
findings.evidence: GameFeatureTests.swift:25-28: `var expected = Game(); expected.play(at: 4)` ... `send(.cellTapped(4)) { $0.game = expected }`. Lines 33-37 send `.cellTapped(4)` and `.cellTapped(99)` and expect no state change. Game.swift:35-36 has an empty play body.
findings.fix: Assert on observable board contents, such as `$0.game.board[4] == .x` or the status text, so a test fails while play is unimplemented, and drop the self-referential expected value. Keep the invalid-tap test in GameCore, where the rules live.
findings.verification_note: Traced the code: with the stub, expected == Game() == actual for any reducer behavior that only calls play, so cellTapPlays and invalidTapsIgnored both pass with forwarding removed or shifted. Verified for this branch. I lowered the severity to minor because the impact is smaller than claimed. Building `expected` with play is not wrong in itself: once ttt-rules makes play real, cellTapPlays catches a dropped tap (Game() vs X at 4) and a shifted index (X at 4 vs X elsewhere). invalidTapsIgnored is aimed at a tap that corrupts the board, not at forwarding, and with real rules it catches a reducer that changes the board. No user-facing outcome.

notes:
GameFeature.State.statusText uses the static helper `GameFeature.State.statusText(outcome: Outcome?, currentPlayer: Player) -> String`. GameFeature reducer: cellTapped(i) calls state.game.play(at:), newGameButtonTapped sets state.game = Game(). AppFeature.State gains `game: GameFeature.State` (init(status:game:) both defaulted) plus `case game(GameFeature.Action)` and a Scope. New AppUI GameView(store: StoreOf<GameFeature>); AppView shows it titled "Tic-tac-toe" and no longer sends .task. UITests/LaunchFlowUITests rewritten for 9 "Empty" cells and "X's turn". GameFeatureTests.swift now also covers .cellTapped (plays square 4; occupied and out-of-range taps leave state unchanged). Slice only builds the area (area.build-only nit), so unit and UI tests were not run by the gate. Tests depend on ttt-rules' Game.
